title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: A classic novel exploring justice and racial injustice in the American South through the eyes of young Scout Finch.

author: George Orwell
description: A dystopian masterpiece that delves into the dangers of totalitarianism, surveillance, and government control.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: A critique of the American Dream and the roaring twenties, told through the disillusioned narrator Nick Carraway.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: A romantic comedy of manners that examines the clash between love, status, and societal expectations.

title: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: The epic fantasy adventure of Bilbo Baggins as he sets out on a quest to reclaim a lost treasure from a dragon.

title: Fahrenheit 451
author: Ray Bradbury
description: A chilling vision of a future society where books are outlawed and firemen burn any that are found.

title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
description: The obsessive quest of Captain Ahab to take revenge on the legendary white whale that destroyed his ship.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J.D. Salinger
description: A poignant exploration of teenage alienation, identity, and loss of innocence, narrated by Holden Caulfield.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
description: A prophetic novel detailing a highly engineered, consumerist future society that trades freedom for superficial happiness.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: An inspiring allegorical novel about an Andalusian shepherd boy who journeys to Egypt in search of a worldly treasure.
